title: Inside Arca's Long-Horizon Agents That Run the Business - Aman Singh, Arca
talk_summary: Arca runs a financial-services firm where agents own long-horizon, stop-start client outcomes end-to-end, with humans pulled in only at decision points. The core mechanism is a signal system: external events (emails, custodian events, market moves) and internal events (human UI actions, task completions) are routed to agents that registered interest, plus scheduled self-wakeups and persistent memory.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents register interest in events ('let me know when Jane responds', 'let me know when that ACH lands'); a background signal system routes incoming events only to interested agents instead of polling or broadcasting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we give them tools to be able to register interest in anything happening in our world

takeaways.technique: Human actions in the UI are signals that wake agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Any human action in the product (rescheduling a calendar event, marking a task complete, adding information) emits a signal that wakes the relevant agent, so agents stay in sync with the internal world without being babysat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when people work in our in our product, when they reschedule a calendar event, you know, that's a signal

takeaways.what_they_do: If an awaited signal never arrives, agents can wake themselves on a schedule to re-check and keep the work moving, so no human has to track it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the signal never lands, agents can like wake themselves up on on a schedule as well to keep track of work

takeaways.technique: Split durable memory from actionable tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly separate state: work that must be remembered for the future goes into agent memory; work doable now becomes a task. Memory persists across the multi-day horizon so context isn't lost between hand-offs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Work that needs to be tracked for the future is tracked in the agent's memory. Work that is doable now becomes a task

takeaways.what_they_do: Because the humans using the product are colleagues, they collect the rich reasoning behind human corrections and turn it into evals for the agent system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we collect rich reasonings from them that become evals for for our system to improve

takeaways.technique: Agents prompt people, not vice versa
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents pre-do ~90% of work and surface a prepared task to the human at the moment of action; new business goals are implemented by adding a goal to the agents' goal set, which then drives work through people.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents prompt people more than people are prompting agents
